faqs.question: What does the LAP Score Test measure?
faqs.answer: The LAP Score Test measures the activity of alkaline phosphatase, an enzyme present in white blood cells, particularly neutrophils.

faqs.question: Why is the LAP Score Test done?
faqs.answer: • To differentiate Chronic Myeloid Leukaemias from Leukaemoid reaction • To make an accurate diagnosis of Chronic Myeloid Leukaemias • To distinguish between benign and malignant leukocytosis • To guide appropriate treatment plans for patients with suspected leukaemia

faqs.question: When is the LAP Score Test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: The LAP Score Test may be recommended if you have • high white blood cell count with an unclear cause, • suspected leukaemia or leukaemia-like symptoms, • previously diagnosed leukaemia to monitor response to treatment, or • a family history of leukaemia or genetic risk factors for haematological disorders.

faqs.question: What if the results of the LAP Score Test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate other hematologic disorders or leukemoid reactions.

faqs.question: What to expect during the LAP Score Test?
faqs.answer: To conduct the test, a blood sample will be collected using a needle from a vein in your arm. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for analysis

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the LAP Score Test?
faqs.answer: • Provide your medical history and any relevant heamato-pathological reports. • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking, as certain drugs may affect test results. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow any other instructions given by your healthcare provider.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the LAP Score Test?
faqs.answer: In addition to the LAP Score Test, Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Bone Marrow Aspiration or Biopsy may be ordered. These tests provide a comprehensive evaluation of blood and bone marrow cells to help diagnose and monitor various haematological conditions.

faqs.question: What is the LAP Score Test also known as?
What is Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia?
faqs.answer: Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia (CML) is a type of cancer that affects the bone marrow and causes an overproduction of abnormal white blood cells. It is often characterised by a specific genetic abnormality called the Philadelphia chromosome. CML can be effectively managed with targeted therapies.
